newsitem.title: UK: IPE and LCH agree automated brokerage system.
newsitem.headline: IPE and LCH agree automated brokerage system.

text.p: The London Clearing House (LCH) and the International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) have agreed on a London-wide automated brokerage project, they said in a joint statement on Tuesday.

"The London trading community has needed something like this for a long time. We are glad that the IPE and LCH have taken the initiative and are developing a system that should benefit all of us," Prudential Bache's Bill Smitt who chairs the working group on the project said in a statement.
LCH and IPE hope that the project will cut costs associated with brokerage operations at the IPE as well as LIFFE.
The scheme will provide centralised arrangements for different members across both Exchanges allowing companies to calculate net brokerage invoices and payments.

"This will allow faster settlement of debts, so reducing borrowing requirements and capital charges. Other benefits iclude time and paperwork savings leading to greater efficiency," the joint statement said.
A prototype of the system, to be developed by the IPE, will ready in trial in November, and the full system is expected to be available by the beginning of 1998. -- London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7714.
